title: Lesson 7: Pest and Disease Control
summary: Learn how to spot common pests and diseases and understand the principles of integrated pest management. Discover safe ways to use pesticides when needed.

sections.heading: Identifying Pests and Diseases
sections.body:
Look for unusual spots, wilting, or holes in leaves. Insects may be visible as bugs, larvae, or webs, while diseases often appear as discoloration or mold.

Use a simple notebook to record what you see, the date, and the part of the plant affected. Comparing your notes with pictures from reliable sources helps confirm the problem.

sections.heading: Integrated Pest Management (IPM)
sections.body:
IPM combines several strategies to keep pests below damaging levels without relying only on chemicals. First, choose resistant crop varieties and rotate crops to break pest life cycles.

Second, encourage natural predators like ladybugs and birds by providing habitats such as flower strips or birdhouses. Finally, use physical controls like traps or row covers when needed.

sections.heading: Safe Pesticide Use
sections.body:
If chemicals are necessary, pick the least toxic option that works for the target pest. Always read the label, wear protective gloves and goggles, and apply only when wind is calm.

Store pesticides out of reach of children and pets, and dispose of empty containers according to local regulations. Keep a record of what you used, where, and when, to avoid over‑application.

key_terms.meaning: A multi‑strategy approach that uses cultural, biological, physical, and chemical methods to control pests.
Changing the type of crop grown in a field each season to reduce pest and disease buildup.
Using living organisms, such as predatory insects or microbes, to suppress pest populations.
The legal document on a pesticide container that lists how to use it safely and effectively.
A plant breed that naturally withstands certain pests or diseases.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a component of Integrated Pest Management?
options: Using the most toxic pesticide available
quiz.why: IPM aims to minimize toxic chemicals, so using the most toxic pesticide contradicts its principles.

quiz.q: What is the first step when you notice a new problem on a plant?
options: Record the symptoms and compare with reliable sources
Ignore it and hope it goes away
quiz.why: Documenting symptoms helps correctly identify the pest or disease before taking action.

quiz.q: Why should you store pesticides out of reach of children and pets?
options: Because they may be used as food
Because they are hazardous if mishandled
quiz.why: Pesticides are toxic and can cause serious harm if accidentally ingested or touched.

quiz.q: Which practice helps attract natural predators to a garden?
options: Planting flower strips and providing birdhouses
quiz.why: Flower strips and birdhouses create habitats that support beneficial insects and birds.

flashcards.front: Name one cultural method used in IPM.
Why is reading the pesticide label important?
flashcards.back: It tells you how to apply safely, the correct dosage, and any restrictions.

flashcards.front: Give an example of biological control.
What should you do before applying a pesticide?
flashcards.back: Monitor the pest, confirm identification, and try non‑chemical controls first.
